description: ni-zav is a software and data-driven team building practical solutions with NASA open data. For the 2026 Space Apps Challenge, we plan to explore TerraLens, an interactive tool for investigating environmental trends, visualizing changes, and evaluating statistical significance. Our focus is reproducible science, intuitive interfaces, and real-world applications, particularly in Indonesia. We welcome collaborators in Earth science, data analysis, and design.
summary: Terra-Lens is an open, auditable Earth-system trend workspace built with authentic NASA data. Users explore 2001–2024 climate and hydrology time series from NASA Giovanni (MERRA-2 reanalysis), live NASA POWER grid points, NASA SWOT satellite river passes, and NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 global anomalies. Instead of drawing naive trend lines across incompatible sources or incomplete years, Terra-Lens computes Gregorian day-weighted complete-year means, pairs classical OLS regression with non-parametric Mann–Kendall and Theil–Sen tests, evaluates shared-year paired differences using Newey–West HAC standard errors, and enforces spatial-support guardrails so regional averages, model grid cells, and satellite reaches are never falsely conflated. Every chart exports self-contained JSON and CSV provenance for independent verification.
details:
What Terra-Lens Does & Why It Matters

Environmental trend claims frequently mislead when dashboards ignore missing months, compare incompatible spatial footprints, or treat two individually "significant" warming lines as proof that one location warmed faster than another. Terra-Lens turns raw NASA satellite and reanalysis records into transparent, reproducible statistical tests with explicit spatial-support and uncertainty guardrails:

  1. Gregorian Day-Weighted Complete-Year Aggregation: Strips NASA sentinel fill values (-999, -9999, 1e15), excludes synthetic annual summary month 13, requires all 12 calendar months per year before computing day-weighted annual means (28/29/30/31 days; 365 vs. 366 in leap years), and requires n >= 10 complete years before reporting trend inference.
  2. Dual Parametric & Non-Parametric Trend Estimation: Reports classical Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) slope (°C/decade or K/decade), two-sided Student-t 95% confidence interval (df = n - 2), and p-value alongside non-parametric Theil–Sen median pairwise slope and tie-corrected Mann–Kendall Z and p, plus residual lag-1 autocorrelation (r_1).
  3. Paired Aligned-Year Difference Testing (B - A): When two series share identical variable, unit, and spatial support, Terra-Lens forms the matched-year difference series d_t = y_{B,t} - y_{A,t} and computes both classical OLS and Newey–West Bartlett kernel HAC standard errors (L = clamp(floor(4(n/100)^(2/9)), 1, 6), L = 2 for n = 24) and Durbin–Watson statistics.
  4. Spatial-Support Guardrails Across Missions: Explicitly distinguishes regional bounding-box averages (NASA Giovanni), single 0.5° x 0.625° model grid cells (NASA POWER), 1D river reaches with pass-level quality flags (NASA SWOT), and global land-ocean anomaly indices (NASA GISS GISTEMP v4)—refusing invalid cross-support difference p-values.
  5. One-Click Auditable Provenance Export: Exports RFC 4180 CSVs (with spreadsheet formula-injection neutralization) and self-contained JSON evidence bundles containing raw monthly records, annual means, test statistics, SHA-256 checksums, and NASA source URLs.

Verified Scientific Findings (2001–2024 · 24 Complete Calendar Years)

All numerical results are independently verified in Python (SciPy, netCDF4, statsmodels) against the JavaScript engine:

  • NASA Giovanni Regional MERRA-2 Case (Official Challenge Resource): Using NASA Giovanni M2TMNXSLV v5.12.4 monthly 2 m air temperature (T2M, doi:10.5067/AP1B0BA5PD2K) averaged over 110°E–111°E, 8°S–7°S (2001–2024, 288 months, 6 model grid cells), the day-weighted annual trend is +0.177171 K/decade (classical 95% CI +0.042313 to +0.312030 K/decade, two-sided p = 0.012376). Independent recomputation from the preserved 6-cell latitude-weighted Giovanni intermediates reproduces all 288 monthly area means within 0.000015 K (float32 precision), and byte-preserved NASA Hyrax OPeNDAP .dap.nc4subsets for all five NASA-reprocessed MERRA2_401 months (2020-09, 2021-06..2021-09) match the Giovanni 6-cell intermediate bit-for-bit (0.0 K max difference).
  • Live NASA POWER Point Trends (Yogyakarta vs. Jakarta Grid Cells): Over 2001–2024 (n = 24), Point A (Yogyakarta grid cell -7.7956°, 110.3695°) warms at +0.179141 °C/decade (95% CI +0.034798 to +0.323484, p = 0.017319; Theil–Sen +0.140943 °C/decade, Mann–Kendall p = 0.023996) and Point B (Jakarta grid cell -6.2088°, 106.8456°) warms at +0.223835 °C/decade (95% CI +0.096212 to +0.351458, p = 0.001455; Theil–Sen +0.192638 °C/decade, Mann–Kendall p = 0.000970).
  • Why Separate P-Values Mislead (Paired Difference Jakarta - Yogyakarta): Although both grid cells warm individually, their paired annual difference slope is +0.044694 °C/decade with a classical OLS 95% CI of -0.072287 to +0.161674 °C/decade (p = 0.436621) and a Newey–West Bartlett lag-2 HAC 95% CI of -0.057416 to +0.146803 °C/decade (HAC SE = 0.004924 °C/year, p = 0.373853, Durbin–Watson 2.21). Because the confidence interval spans zero, the data do not establish that the Jakarta grid cell warmed faster than the Yogyakarta grid cell.
  • Cross-Source Context Cases: Juxtaposes 12 irregular SWOT L2 RiverSP vD overpasses on Ohio River reach 74267300251 (120.68–131.25 m, 10 suspect reach_q = 1 and 2 degraded reach_q = 2 passes) with 3 overlapping months of NASA POWER precipitation (3.99 / 7.08 / 4.04 mm/day), refusing a 3-month correlation p-value; and compares rebased 2001–2020 Yogyakarta POWER anomalies (+0.1791 °C/decade) against NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 global anomalies (+0.2504 °C/decade, descriptive gap -0.0713 °C/decade) and NASA's Giovanni MERRA-2 summer heatwave frequency (HWF, 1980–2023) tutorial series.

Explicit Scientific & Data Limitations

  • Grid support != urban thermometer: MERRA-2 and NASA POWER represent 0.5° x 0.625° model reanalysis grid cells or regional bounding-box means, not neighborhood weather stations or population heat exposure.
  • Historical description != causal attribution or forecast: Fitted slopes summarize past trajectory in the selected window only.
  • Giovanni lineage & QA boundaries: The preserved Giovanni M2TMNXSLV v5.12.4 export and native monthly granules carry no per-cell quality-flag variable, and while the 6-cell values in the 5 reprocessed months match MERRA2_401 OPeNDAP .dap.nc4 granules bit-for-bit, the Giovanni aggregate file itself does not embed a native GranuleID manifest.
  • Exploratory screening: Post-selected pairs from the 8-point Indonesian Trend Contrast Finder (28 candidate pairs) and 12-month seasonal scans are labeled as exploratory hypothesis generation because multiple testing is not adjusted.
